title: The Question at 3 AM
description:
Ceiling of the gosiwon. 3 AM. The fan whirring.

He did something today. Worked on a resume, checked stocks, ran an errand. But he can't quite say what.

"Is this right?"

choices.text: It is. This is the best I can do right now.
choices.result_text:
It wasn't a question with an answer. But he decided to answer it that way.

The fact that he was asking this at 3 AM, staring at the ceiling — that itself was proof he was doing something.

choices.text: I don't know. I should just sleep.
choices.result_text:
He turned off the light. Questions without answers are better left to morning.

Maybe that was an answer too.

title: The Old Notebook
description:
Sorting through boxes, he found a notebook from his first year of university.

"Build a company with my name on it within 10 years. Change the world by 30."

The handwriting back then was bolder than now.

choices.text: That version of me wasn't wrong. Just the direction shifted.
choices.result_text:
He closed the notebook. Didn't throw it out.

Changing the world might be quieter and slower than he thought back then. Past-him wasn't wrong — just didn't know yet.

choices.text: That version of me didn't know. How the world actually works.
choices.result_text:
He slipped the notebook back into the box. That old handwriting felt lonely.

Not knowing isn't a crime. But he envied that ignorance.

title: Why Gangnam
description:
Someone asked, "Why Gangnam?"

Simple question. He stalled.
Because it's expensive? Because arriving there means succeeding? Just because that's the dream?

He couldn't find the words.

choices.text: "Gangnam is a benchmark. Wherever I can live at that level."
choices.result_text:
It made sense as he said it.

It's not about living in Gangnam — it's about becoming someone who can. Not about changing the number, but about becoming someone who can make that number.

choices.text: "I want to live in Gangnam. That's the goal."
choices.result_text:
An honest answer.

Calling a desire a desire, without embarrassment. That alone made something feel clearer.

title: Me at 43
description:
He paused his pen over a cafe notebook.

Five years to 38. So where does 43 find him?
Planning the next target from Gangnam? Or still in the middle of another battle?

The picture wouldn't form.

choices.text: He wrote down where he wants to be at 43. (mapped it out)
choices.result_text:
A few lines. Rough, but better than nothing.

When you can see five years ahead, today changes. People with direction and people without it spend the same hour very differently.

choices.text: After 38, he'll figure it out. Right now comes first.
choices.result_text:
He closed the notebook. Staying present is also a strategy.

He wasn't going to lose 33 chasing 43.

title: Defining Success
description:
A KakaoTalk from an army buddy. Made executive. Photos: nice car, wide office.

He sent "Congrats" and put the phone down.

For a moment, he thought about it. What does success mean to me?

choices.text: 3 billion. Gangnam. I have a number.
choices.result_text:
A concrete number beats an abstract ideal.

He might not know what 'executive' means for himself, but he knows what 3 billion means. The account balance will prove it.

choices.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. Not yet.
choices.result_text:
Not knowing was the answer.

Trying to define success by watching someone else's — that was the wrong starting point. He'd get to 3 billion first and ask again then.
